facts.status_note: FFLA statewide list marks the tower Tower Gone; the 2011 chapter report says it was removed as part of the MSCommNet Project

events.note: Maine Forestry Service 360-degree panoramic map dated 1920 is centered on the May Mt. fire tower in Island Falls; the map does not give a build date

corrections.current: Steel-only tower was removed for the MSCommNet radio tower and judged not salvageable
corrections.proposed: Removed as part of the MSCommNet Project, a statewide radio upgrade. Steel-only construction and a radio-tower replacement are not stated in the sources read.
corrections.why: The 2011 chapter report says May Mountain was removed as part of the MSCommNet Project. It does not describe the structure as steel-only or say the site was cleared to make way for a radio tower.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: no construction date, staffing or fire history in any source read, and no current site description. The FFLA Maine chapter Facebook post appeared only as a search snippet (the page would not load); it reportedly gives a 1920 build, staffing to the end of 1969, a 1988 reopening with a watch lady, and removal in June 2011. Unverified and not used; worth checking. Another search snippet describes a former May Mountain ski area near Island Pond, a different place, not used. The 2011 report's salvage wording spans a line break, so it is not quoted. Correction above covers the brief's steel-only and radio-tower wording.
